Visit note | 2025-10-29 12:30 PM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Bilkis Haque, 58, female. Mrs. Haque returns for review, reporting headaches on waking and a high reading on a pharmacy machine. She works as a rickshaw puller and her elevated pressure was first found during a free health camp in Farmgate. She reports no chest pain or shortness of breath. On examination: BP 145/97 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 59 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no added sounds. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check her blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2025-10-29 12:30 PM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Lamia Munshi, 46, female. Ms. Munshi presents for her first visit complaining of a painful red lump at the edge of the eyelid and swelling of the eyelid. She works as a hotel receptionist and notes the lump appeared during a stressful week in Lalbagh. She denies any visual changes or discharge. On examination: lump about 7 mm on the left upper eyelid, BP 128/75 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 62 kg. Assessment: Hordeolum. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to use a warm compress four times a day, avoid squeezing the lump, and avoid eye makeup. Follow-up in 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-10-29 03:00 PM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Arifa Bhuiyan, 46, female. Mrs. Bhuiyan attends for a review visit, stating she has been experiencing aching all over the body, a mild headache, and fever for two to three days. She works as a construction worker and her symptoms started after getting soaked in heavy rain in Motijheel. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She reports no cough or sore throat. On examination: temperature 102.2°F, BP 113/84 mmHg, pulse 93 bpm, weight 47 kg. Chest is clear and abdomen is soft. Assessment: Viral fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink plenty of fluids, rest at home for three days, and sponge with lukewarm water if the fever is high. Follow-up in 3 days if the fever does not settle.

Visit note | 2025-10-29 03:00 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Mahiya Faruque, 68, female. Visit note | 2025-10-29 03:00 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Afsana Molla, 74, female. Mrs. Molla comes in for a review visit, reporting that she is always feeling cold and has dry skin. Visit note | 2025-10-29 03:00 PM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Kawsar Hossain, 25, male. Mr. Hossain attends for a follow-up appointment regarding chronic skin issues. He reports that his symptoms are notably worse in winter, with severe scratching at night and itchy dry patches on the elbows and knees. He works as a rickshaw puller and mentions the condition started after working with cleaning chemicals in Wari. He has no significant past medical history and denies any systemic symptoms like fever or joint pain. On examination, the affected area is about 10 cm across with lichenified plaques and excoriations over the bilateral elbows and knees. Other vitals show a blood pressure of 114/74 mmHg, pulse of 78 bpm, and weight of 53 kg. The remaining skin examination is clear. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: a prescription was issued for topical emollients and mild steroids. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes to prevent further irritation. Follow-up in 2 weeks to assess treatment response.
